import html # Predefined HTML template with placeholders. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {event_title}

{event_title}

Date: {event_date}

{event_description}
Notes: {additional_notes}
""" def create_event_invitation(title: str, description: str, date: str, notes: str) -> str: """ Generate a secure HTML invitation for an event. Parameters ---------- title : str The title or name of the event. description : str A comprehensive description of the event (may include multiple paragraphs and formatting). date : str The scheduled date of the event. notes : str Any supplementary information or instructions provided by the event organizer. Returns ------- str Sanitized HTML string ready for safe rendering in a browser. Raises ------ ValueError If any required argument is missing or empty. """ # Validate inputs if not all(isinstance(arg, str) for arg in (title, description, date, notes)): raise TypeError("All arguments must be strings.") if not title.strip(): raise ValueError("Event title cannot be empty.") # Escape user-supplied content to prevent XSS and other injection attacks safe_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) safe_description = html.escape(description, quote=False).replace('\n', '
') safe_date = html.escape(date, quote=True) safe_notes = html.escape(notes, quote=False).replace('\n', '
') # Render the invitation using the template rendered = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_title=safe_title, event_description=safe_description, event_date=safe_date, additional_notes=safe_notes ) return rendered.strip()
